_doc: What tools/site.mjs ships: programs whose code AND data may be redistributed by a third party, each with its licences. `program` is a web/programs/*.json descriptor, `machine` the shelf it sits on (web/machines.json), `licenseFiles` what is copied beside it (`path` in the repository, corpus included, or `from: data` for a file under --games). A program is added here only once both licences have been READ on disk, not remembered: 2026-10-13 audit. Tux Racer's data states no licence; its author's SourceForge project publishes it under the GPL v2 (tools/site-licenses/tuxracer-data.txt). Left out for now: morph3d (no licence in its file), Tyrian 2.1 (its own file_id.diz forbids distribution), SDLPoP, Keen Dreams (proprietary data, or shareware terms that forbid it). Quake's shareware is shipped as its ARCHIVE (quake106.zip, its RESOURCE.1 an LHA that web/unpack.js opens): its licence allows passing the archive on whole, and forbids showing the game's screens, so Quake and its gallery siblings have a title card (thumb.card, tools/title-card.mjs), never a screenshot. Doom's shareware is shipped as its ARCHIVE, unmodified, as its terms allow (web/unpack.js); So is Cube's (its readme: "you may freely distribute the cube archive unmodified on any media"), a tar.gz unpacked in the page. So is Heretic's: its source is GPL since 2008 (Raven's release on SourceForge is byte-identical to the tree PRISM compiles).

programs.author: Brian Paul
programs.blurb: Two textured squares, each with its own texture object, spinning.

args: local r=' .,:;-=+*#%@' for y=-11,11 do local s='' for x=-39,38 do local cr,ci,zr,zi,i=x/30-0.65,y/10,0,0,0 while i<200 and zr*zr+zi*zi<4 do zr,zi=zr*zr-zi*zi+cr,2*zr*zi+ci i=i+1 end local k=i==200 and 12 or math.min(11,math.floor(math.log(i,2))+1) s=s..r:sub(k,k) end print(s) end
